records.literal_gloss: These [are the] generations of the heavens and the earth in their being created, in [the] day of making [by] YHWH God earth and heavens.

en.L: These [are] the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made earth and heavens.
en.B: This is the story of the heavens and the earth as they were created. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made earth and heavens,
en.R: This is the story of how the heavens and the earth came to be. It begins at the time when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the earth and the sky.

es.L: Estas [son] las generaciones de los cielos y de la tierra cuando fueron creados, el día en que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo la tierra y los cielos.
es.B: Esta es la historia de los cielos y la tierra cuando fueron creados. Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo la tierra y los cielos,

fr.L: Voici les générations des cieux et de la terre lorsqu’ils furent créés, au jour où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu fit terre et cieux.
fr.B: Voici l’histoire des cieux et de la terre, tels qu’ils furent créés. Lorsque {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu fit la terre et les cieux,
fr.R: Voici l’histoire de la manière dont le ciel et la terre sont venus à l’existence. Elle commence au moment où {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a fait la terre et le ciel.

sw.L: Hivi [ni] vizazi vya mbingu na dunia wakati zilipoumbwa, katika siku ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu alifanya dunia na mbingu.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo habari ya mbingu na dunia jinsi zilivyoumbwa. Wakati {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu alipofanya dunia na mbingu,

vi.L: Đây [là] dòng dõi của trời và đất khi chúng được sáng tạo, vào ngày {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm ra đất và trời.

vi.R: Đây là câu chuyện về cách trời và đất đã có. Câu chuyện bắt đầu vào lúc {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm ra đất và bầu trời.

ko.L: 하늘과 땅이 창조될 때, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅과 하늘을 만드신 날에, 하늘과 땅의 계보는 이러하다.
ko.B: 하늘과 땅이 창조된 이야기는 이러하다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅과 하늘을 만드실 때에,
ko.R: 하늘과 땅이 생겨난 이야기는 이러하다. 이 이야기는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅과 하늘을 만드실 때에 시작된다.

pt.L: Estas [são] as gerações dos céus e da terra quando foram criados, no dia em que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez terra e céus.
pt.B: Esta é a história dos céus e da terra, de como foram criados. Quando {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez a terra e os céus,
pt.R: Esta é a história de como os céus e a terra vieram a existir. Ela começa no tempo em que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez a terra e o céu.

decisions.choice: generations: an account of what came from them
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to father, to give birth" and usually introduces a family line (5:1; 10:1). Genesis uses "these are the generations of ..." ten times to open a new section, which tells what came from the one named rather than how it began. Here it introduces what came from the heavens and the earth: the story of the man and the woman that follows.

decisions.choice: the first half heads the new account; the second half begins its first sentence
alternatives: the first half closes the account of the seven days (1:1-2:3)
decisions.reason: Everywhere else in Genesis "these are the generations of" opens a section, so the first half of the verse most likely heads the story that follows. Many readers take it instead as the close of 1:1-2:3, since "the heavens and the earth" and "created" echo 1:1. The two halves mirror each other: "the heavens and the earth ... created", then "earth and heavens ... made". The second half begins a sentence that runs to verse 7.

decisions.choice: the LORD: YHWH, the personal name of God
decisions.reason: Here, for the first time, God is called by his own name, written with four consonants, YHWH. Exodus 3:14-15 links it with the verb "to be". In time Jewish readers stopped saying the name aloud out of reverence and read "Lord" in its place; the Hebrew manuscripts carry the vowels of that word, and the Septuagint translates the name "Lord". How the name was first pronounced is not recorded; Yahweh is the form most scholars reconstruct.

decisions.choice: the LORD God: the name joined with the title God
decisions.reason: Chapters 2 and 3 join the name and "God" again and again, a pairing that is rare elsewhere. It tells the reader that the God of chapter 1, maker of everything, is the LORD, the God who later makes himself known to Israel by name (Exodus 6:2-3), and who here deals closely with the man and the woman.

decisions.choice: the LORD (default); Yahweh (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: Following long custom, the name is written "the LORD" in capital letters, to set it apart from the title "Lord" (m3). The divine name setting shows "Yahweh" instead. "Jehovah", an older form, combines the consonants of the name with the vowels of the word for Lord.

decisions.choice: the story of
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "generations". Balanced and Readable say "story", since here the word introduces an account of what followed (m1).

decisions.choice: el SEÑOR (default); Yahvé (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: As in English (r-en-1), the name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals, following long custom, to set it apart from the title "Señor" (m3); at the start of a sentence it is "El SEÑOR". The divine name setting shows "Yahvé", the usual Spanish form of the name in scholarship (also spelled "Yahveh" or "Yavé"). "Jehová", familiar to Spanish readers from the Reina-Valera tradition, joins the consonants of the name to the vowels of the word for Lord, and is not used. Because a personal name takes no article in Spanish, the setting span takes in the article and its contractions with a preposition: "el SEÑOR" / "Yahvé", "del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé". This holds throughout the book.

decisions.choice: le SEIGNEUR (default); Yahvé (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Genesis and the Pentateuch. As in English (r-en-1), the name is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, to set it apart from the title "Seigneur" (m3); at the start of a sentence it is "Le SEIGNEUR". The divine name setting shows "Yahvé", the usual French form of the reconstructed name. "L'Éternel", the rendering of the Segond tradition, is a form a reviewer may prefer: it echoes the link with the verb "to be" (Exodus 3:14) but is a title rather than the name, and it is not the default. Since a name takes no article in French, the span takes in the article and its contractions: "le SEIGNEUR" / "Yahvé", "du SEIGNEUR" / "de Yahvé", "au SEIGNEUR" / "à Yahvé". "The LORD God" is "le SEIGNEUR Dieu", and Adonai YHWH "le Seigneur DIEU".

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("fit", "forma"); passé composé at Readable ("a fait")
decisions.reason: The tense choice for French narrative in Genesis, recorded in 1:1: the passé simple of written narrative at Literal and Balanced, the passé composé of spoken French at Readable.

decisions.choice: BWANA (default); Yahwe (divine name setting)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Genesis and the Pentateuch. As in English (r-en-1), the name is written "BWANA" in capitals, to set it apart from the title "Bwana" (m3). The divine name setting shows "Yahwe", the reconstructed form of the name in Swahili spelling. "Yehova", known to Swahili readers from some churches, joins the consonants of the name to the vowels of the word for Lord, and is not used. Swahili has no article, so the span is the name alone; "the LORD God" is "BWANA Mungu", and Adonai YHWH "Bwana MUNGU".

decisions.choice: "CHÚA Đức Chúa Trời" by default, "Gia-vê Đức Chúa Trời" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: The divine name YHWH is written "CHÚA" in capitals, as the English writes "the LORD", with the name "Gia-vê" as the setting's alternative; it is joined to the title "Đức Chúa Trời" (God), as the Hebrew joins them (m4). The older form "Giê-hô-va" is not used.

decisions.choice: "Đây [là] dòng dõi của" (L), "Đây là câu chuyện về" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The heading toledot introduces an account of what came from someone (m1). As the Genesis terms note settles: Literal keeps the word for descendants, Balanced and Readable say "the story of"; here it is the heavens and the earth, not a family, so "dòng họ" is not added.

decisions.choice: A divine_name span for YHWH: 주 by default, 야훼 with the setting, followed by 하나님 for "the LORD God"
decisions.reason: As the terms note and the style guide (section 7a): YHWH is "주" by default and "야훼" with the divine name setting; the particle stands outside the span, since both forms end in a vowel. "여호와", the form of older Protestant Bibles, is not used. With Elohim the pair is "주 하나님". This holds for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "계보는 이러하다" (L); "이야기는 이러하다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note settles "~의 계보는 이러하다" at Literal and "~의 집안 이야기" at Balanced and Readable for the headings of the book's sections. The heavens and the earth have no family, so here Balanced and Readable say only "이야기", the story of what came from them (meaning decision m1). The other headings (5:1; 6:9; 10:1; 11:10; 11:27) follow the note.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus: "o SENHOR" by default, "Javé" with the divine name setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md sets it. The name is written "SENHOR" in capitals, as Portuguese Bibles have long done, to set it apart from the title "Senhor" (m3); the setting shows "Javé", the usual Brazilian form of the name. The article goes inside the span ("o SENHOR" / "Javé", "do SENHOR" / "de Javé"), since "o Javé" is not Portuguese. "Jeová" mixes the consonants of the name with the vowels of the word for Lord and is not used.

source.text: וְכֹ֣ל׀שִׂ֣יחַ הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה טֶ֚רֶם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֔רֶץ וְכָל־עֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה טֶ֣רֶם יִצְמָ֑ח כִּי֩ לֹ֨א הִמְטִ֜יר יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאָדָ֣ם אַ֔יִן לַֽעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And every shrub of the field not yet was in the earth, and every plant of the field not yet sprouted, for not had caused rain YHWH God on the earth, and [a] human there was not to work the ground,

en.L: and no shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprouted, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had not caused it to rain on the earth, and there was no human to work the ground,
en.B: no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no one to work the ground.
en.R: There were no bushes or crops growing in the fields yet. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God had not sent any rain on the earth, and there was no one to farm the land.

es.L: y aún no había en la tierra ningún arbusto del campo, y aún no había brotado ninguna planta del campo, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios no había hecho llover sobre la tierra, y no había ningún ser humano que trabajara el suelo,

fr.L: et il n’y avait encore sur la terre aucun buisson de la campagne, et aucune plante de la campagne n’avait encore poussé, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu n’avait pas envoyé la pluie sur la terre, et il n’y avait pas d’être humain pour travailler le sol,
fr.B: aucun buisson des champs n’avait encore paru sur la terre, et aucune plante des champs n’avait encore levé, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu n’avait pas fait tomber la pluie sur la terre, et qu’il n’y avait personne pour travailler le sol.

vi.L: và chưa có một bụi cây nào của đồng ruộng trên đất, và chưa có một cây cỏ nào của đồng ruộng mọc lên, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chưa cho mưa xuống trên đất, và không có con người để cày cấy đất,
vi.B: chưa có bụi cây nào ngoài đồng xuất hiện trên đất, và chưa có cây cỏ nào ngoài đồng mọc lên, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chưa cho mưa xuống trên đất, và cũng không có ai để cày cấy đất.
vi.R: Lúc ấy chưa có bụi cây hay hoa màu nào mọc trong đồng ruộng. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời chưa cho mưa xuống trên đất, và cũng chưa có ai để trồng trọt đất đai.

ko.L: 그리고 들의 덤불이 아직 땅에 하나도 없었고, 들의 풀도 아직 하나도 돋지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅 위에 비를 내리지 않으셨고, 땅을 일굴 사람도 없었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 들에는 아직 덤불 하나 땅에 나지 않았고, 밭의 풀도 아직 돋아나지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에 비를 내리지 않으셨고, 땅을 일굴 사람도 없었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 들에는 아직 덤불도 곡식도 자라지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 아직 땅에 비를 내리지 않으셨고, 땅에 농사를 지을 사람도 없었다.

pt.L: e nenhum arbusto do campo ainda havia na terra, e nenhuma planta do campo ainda tinha brotado, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus não tinha feito chover sobre a terra, e não havia ser humano para trabalhar o solo,
pt.B: nenhum arbusto do campo tinha surgido ainda na terra, e nenhuma planta do campo tinha brotado, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus não tinha mandado chuva sobre a terra, e não havia ninguém para cultivar o solo.
pt.R: Ainda não havia arbustos nem plantações crescendo nos campos. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus ainda não tinha mandado chuva sobre a terra, e não havia ninguém para cultivar a terra.

decisions.choice: shrub of the field, plant of the field: wild bushes, and crops that need someone to grow them
decisions.reason: The account names two kinds of growth that are missing: wild shrubs, which need rain, and the plants of the field, the crops people grow (3:18 uses the same words for the food the man will grow). Each lack is matched by its cause: no rain, and no one to work the ground. The verse does not speak of all plant life, and so does not contradict 1:11-12; it describes a land not yet farmed.

decisions.choice: a human to work the ground: adam and adamah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on the human (adam) and the ground (adamah): the land waits for someone to work it, and in verse 7 the human is formed from it. The verb "work" is used again in 2:15 and 3:23; it also means "serve".

decisions.choice: no shrub ... yet
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "every shrub ... not yet was"; English says "no shrub ... yet".

decisions.choice: la tierra (the earth); el suelo (the ground)
decisions.reason: Spanish "tierra" would serve for both Hebrew words, the earth and the ground. Literal and Balanced keep "la tierra" for the earth and say "el suelo" for the ground that the human works and is formed from (m2), so that the link between the two stays visible through chapters 2 and 3. Readable says "la tierra" or "el campo" where that is plainer.

decisions.choice: kichaka cha porini ... mmea wa shambani
decisions.reason: The two kinds of growth are wild bushes and the crops people grow (m1). Swahili "shamba" is a cultivated field, so Balanced says "porini" (in the wild) for the bushes and keeps "shambani" for the crops; Literal keeps "shambani" for both, as the Hebrew uses one word.

decisions.choice: "con người" ... "đất"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sounds adam (human) against adamah (ground) (m2). Vietnamese cannot keep the sound; the meaning decision explains it.

source.text: וְאֵ֖ד יַֽעֲלֶ֣ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִשְׁקָ֖ה אֶֽת־כָּל־פְּנֵֽי־הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and a stream went up from the earth and watered all [the] face of the ground.

en.L: and a stream would go up from the earth and water the whole face of the ground.
en.B: Instead, water would well up from the earth and soak the whole surface of the ground.
en.R: But water came up out of the ground and watered all the land.

es.L: y una corriente subía de la tierra y regaba toda la faz del suelo.
es.B: En cambio, el agua brotaba de la tierra y empapaba toda la superficie del suelo.
es.R: Pero el agua salía de la tierra y regaba todo el campo.

fr.L: et un flot montait de la terre et arrosait toute la face du sol.
fr.B: Mais de l’eau jaillissait de la terre et imbibait toute la surface du sol.
fr.R: Mais de l’eau sortait de la terre et arrosait tous les champs.

sw.L: na mkondo wa maji ulikuwa ukipanda kutoka duniani na kuunywesha uso wote wa ardhi.
sw.B: Badala yake, maji yalikuwa yakibubujika kutoka chini ya dunia na kulowesha uso wote wa ardhi.
sw.R: Lakini maji yalikuwa yakitoka ardhini na kunywesha nchi yote.

vi.L: và một dòng nước thường dâng lên từ đất và tưới khắp mặt đất.
vi.B: Nhưng nước thường từ đất trào lên và thấm ướt khắp mặt đất.
vi.R: Nhưng nước từ dưới đất trào lên và tưới khắp đất đai.

ko.L: 그리고 땅에서 물줄기가 솟아올라 땅의 온 표면을 적시곤 했다.
ko.B: 대신 땅에서 물이 솟아올라 온 땅의 표면을 흠뻑 적시곤 했다.
ko.R: 그러나 땅속에서 물이 솟아 나와 온 땅을 적셔 주었다.

pt.L: e uma corrente de água subia da terra e regava toda a face do solo.
pt.B: Em vez disso, a água brotava da terra e encharcava toda a superfície do solo.
pt.R: Mas a água saía do chão e molhava toda a terra.

decisions.choice: a flow of water rising from the earth
decisions.reason: The word is rare; it is used again only in Job 36:27, where it is linked with rain. Older translations said "mist". A similar word in Akkadian means the flood of a river, and rising "from the earth" suits water welling up from below, like the deep waters of 7:11 and 49:25. Either way, the ground is watered before anyone works it.

decisions.choice: would go up, would water: something that happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a repeated or ongoing action in the past, setting the scene for verse 7.

decisions.choice: subía ... regaba (imperfect)
decisions.reason: The Spanish imperfect says by itself what English needs "would" for: something that happened again and again (m2).

decisions.choice: imparfait: montait ... arrosait (L), jaillissait ... imbibait (B), sortait ... arrosait (R)
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what happened again and again (m2), which French says with the imperfect at every level, inside a narrative otherwise in the passé simple or the passé composé.

decisions.choice: uma corrente de água (L); a água (B, R)
decisions.reason: The older Portuguese Bibles say "neblina" or "vapor", as older English says "mist"; the word more likely means water welling up from below (m1), so Portuguese says so, as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּיצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֗ם עָפָר֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וַיִּפַּ֥ח בְּאַפָּ֖יו נִשְׁמַ֣ת חַיִּ֑ים וַֽיְהִ֥י הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְנֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And formed YHWH God the man, dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils breath of life, and became the man a living creature.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed the man, dust from the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God shaped the man out of dust from the ground. He breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made a man out of dust from the ground, like a potter shaping clay. He breathed the breath of life into the man's nose, and the man came to life.

es.L: Y formó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios al hombre, polvo del suelo, y sopló en sus narices aliento de vida, y llegó a ser el hombre una criatura viviente.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios moldeó al hombre con polvo del suelo. Le sopló en la nariz el aliento de vida, y el hombre se convirtió en un ser viviente.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo un hombre con polvo del suelo, como un alfarero que modela el barro. Le sopló en la nariz el aliento de vida, y el hombre empezó a vivir.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu forma l’homme, poussière [prise] du sol, et souffla dans ses narines un souffle de vie, et l’homme devint un être vivant.
fr.B: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu façonna l’homme avec de la poussière du sol. Il lui insuffla dans les narines le souffle de vie, et l’homme devint un être vivant.
fr.R: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a fait un homme avec de la poussière du sol, comme un potier qui façonne l’argile. Il a soufflé dans le nez de l’homme pour lui donner le souffle de vie, et l’homme a commencé à vivre.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamfinyanga mtu, mavumbi kutoka ardhini, akapuliza ndani ya pua zake pumzi ya uhai, na mtu huyo akawa kiumbe hai.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamfinyanga mtu kwa mavumbi ya ardhi. Akapuliza pumzi ya uhai ndani ya pua zake, naye mtu akawa kiumbe hai.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamfanya mtu kwa mavumbi ya ardhi, kama mfinyanzi anavyofinyanga udongo. Akapuliza pumzi ya uhai ndani ya pua za mtu huyo, naye akaanza kuishi.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời nắn con người, [bằng] bụi từ đất, và thổi vào lỗ mũi người hơi thở của sự sống, và con người trở nên một sinh vật sống.
vi.B: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời nắn con người từ bụi đất. Ngài thổi hơi thở của sự sống vào lỗ mũi người, và con người trở nên một sinh vật sống.
vi.R: Rồi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời lấy bụi đất làm nên một người đàn ông, như người thợ gốm nắn đất sét. Ngài thổi hơi thở của sự sống vào mũi người ấy, và người ấy bắt đầu sống.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅의 흙으로 그 사람을 빚으시고, 그의 콧구멍에 생명의 숨을 불어넣으시니, 그 사람이 살아 있는 생물이 되었다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅의 흙으로 그 사람을 빚으시고, 그의 코에 생명의 숨을 불어넣으셨다. 그러자 그 사람이 살아 있는 존재가 되었다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅의 흙으로 사람을 만드셨다. 토기장이가 진흙을 빚듯이 빚으셨다. 그리고 그 사람의 코에 생명의 숨을 불어넣으시자, 그 사람이 살아났다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus formou o homem, pó do solo, e soprou nas narinas dele o fôlego de vida, e o homem se tornou um ser vivente.
pt.B: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus modelou o homem com pó do solo. Ele soprou nas narinas dele o fôlego de vida, e o homem se tornou um ser vivo.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez um homem com pó do chão, como um oleiro que modela o barro. Ele soprou o fôlego de vida no nariz do homem, e o homem ganhou vida.

decisions.choice: formed: shaped, as a potter shapes clay
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a potter at work (Jeremiah 18:2-6; Isaiah 64:8). Chapter 1 tells of God's word; this account shows his hands, shaping the man as a potter shapes a pot.

decisions.choice: the man: the first human, formed from the ground
alternatives: the human, not yet male or female
decisions.reason: He is called "the human" (ha-adam), a play on "the ground" (ha-adamah) that he is formed from. With the article the word is not yet a personal name. The story treats him as one person, and when the woman is made from him he calls himself "man" (ish, verse 23).

decisions.choice: the breath of life: life given by God's own breath
decisions.reason: The man's life comes from God's breath, given to no other creature in the account. The phrase returns in 7:22. "Living creature" is the phrase used of the animals in 1:20-24: the man is alive as they are, but he received his life directly from God.

decisions.choice: shaped
decisions.reason: Balanced says "shaped" to keep the picture of the potter (m1).

decisions.choice: like a potter shaping clay
decisions.reason: Readable adds the picture of the potter to show what "formed" means (m1).

decisions.choice: el hombre ... del suelo
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on the human (adam) and the ground (adamah) he is formed from (m2). Spanish has no pair that keeps the sound without strain: "terroso" (earthy) or "humano" / "humus" make the play but sound contrived or technical, and "humus" today means rich topsoil. All levels say "el hombre" and "el suelo", the word kept for the ground throughout (see 2:5), and leave the play to the meaning note.

decisions.choice: l'homme ... du sol, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Here the word names one person, the first man (m2), so French says "l'homme" without the gender setting, as the English says "the man". French cannot keep the Hebrew play between the human and the ground (adam, adamah); "le sol" is kept for the ground, as in 1:25. "Être vivant" is the phrase used for the animals in 1:20-24 (m3).

decisions.choice: akamfinyanga
decisions.reason: "Kufinyanga" is the potter's verb, shaping clay by hand, which is what the Hebrew pictures (m1). Readable says "akamfanya" and adds the potter ("kama mfinyanzi anavyofinyanga udongo"), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "con người" (L, B), "người đàn ông" (R) for ha-adam in chapters 2–3
decisions.reason: The man is one particular person but is not yet given the name Adam; "người nam" is kept for ish in 2:23–24. Literal and Balanced say "con người" (the human), which keeps the link with all humankind; Readable says "người đàn ông", as the English Readable says "a man".

decisions.choice: "그 사람" for the man, "땅" for the ground
decisions.reason: Through chapters 2 and 3 the Hebrew calls him "the man", a word that sounds like the word for the ground he is made from (meaning decision m2 here and at 2:5). Korean cannot keep the echo; it says "그 사람", not yet the name 아담, as the English says "the man".

decisions.choice: "살아 있는 존재" (B)
decisions.reason: 1 Corinthians 15:45 quotes these words in the Korean New Testament as "살아 있는 존재"; Balanced uses the same words. Literal says "살아 있는 생물", the words used for the animals in chapter 1, since the Hebrew phrase is the same. "생령" is the word of older Bibles.

decisions.choice: o homem (no gender setting)
decisions.reason: For chapters 2 and 3: here the word is "the human", one person, formed from the ground (m2), so Portuguese says "o homem", as the English says "the man", with no gender setting. It is not yet the name Adão, which Portuguese uses only where the English does. Literal and Balanced keep "o solo" for the ground, as in 1:25, so that the link between the man and the ground can be seen.

decisions.choice: modelou
decisions.reason: "Modelar" is what a potter does with clay, so Balanced keeps the picture of the potter (m1), as the English Balanced says "shaped".

source.text: וַיִּטַּ֞ע יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים גַּן־בְעֵ֖דֶן מִקֶּ֑דֶם וַיָּ֣שֶׂם שָׁ֔ם אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And planted YHWH God a garden in Eden from [the] east, and put there the man whom he had formed.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put there the man whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had formed.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} placed the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shaped.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God planted a garden in a place called Eden, in the east. He put the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made there.

es.L: Y plantó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios un jardín en Edén, al oriente, y puso allí al hombre que había formado.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios plantó un jardín en Edén, hacia el oriente, y allí colocó al hombre que había moldeado.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios plantó un jardín en un lugar llamado Edén, en el oriente. Allí puso al hombre que había hecho.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu planta un jardin en Éden, à l’orient, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} plaça là l’homme qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait formé.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu planta un jardin en Éden, vers l’est, et c’est là qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} installa l’homme qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait façonné.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a planté un jardin dans un pays appelé Éden, à l’est. Il y a mis l’homme qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akapanda bustani katika Edeni, upande wa mashariki, akamweka humo mtu aliyekuwa amemfinyanga.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akapanda bustani katika Edeni, kuelekea mashariki, na huko akamweka yule mtu aliyemfinyanga.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akapanda bustani mahali palipoitwa Edeni, upande wa mashariki. Akamweka humo yule mtu aliyekuwa amemfanya.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời trồng một khu vườn ở Ê-đen, về phía đông, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt ở đó con người mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nắn nên.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời trồng một khu vườn ở Ê-đen, về phía đông, và ở đó {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt con người mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nắn nên.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời trồng một khu vườn ở một nơi gọi là Ê-đen, về phía đông. Ngài đặt người đàn ông mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm nên ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 동쪽 에덴에 동산을 심으시고, 자신이 빚으신 그 사람을 거기에 두셨다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 동쪽에 있는 에덴에 동산을 일구시고, 빚으신 그 사람을 그곳에 두셨다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 동쪽에 있는 에덴이라는 곳에 동산을 가꾸셨다. 그리고 만드신 그 사람을 그곳에 두셨다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus plantou um jardim no Éden, do lado do oriente, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pôs lá o homem que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha formado.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus plantou um jardim no Éden, para os lados do leste, e ali colocou o homem que tinha modelado.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus plantou um jardim num lugar chamado Éden, no leste. Ele pôs ali o homem que tinha feito.

decisions.choice: Eden: a region, with the garden in it
decisions.reason: Eden sounds like a Hebrew word for delight or plenty. The garden is planted in Eden and is not the same as Eden: a river flows out of Eden to water the garden (verse 10).

decisions.choice: in the east: toward the east
alternatives: in ancient times, at the beginning
decisions.reason: The word can mean the east or long ago (Psalm 74:12). Here it places the garden toward the east, as later the way back to it lies to the east (3:24; 4:16).

decisions.choice: jardín
decisions.reason: "Huerto", the older word in Spanish Bibles, now suggests a vegetable plot. The garden is a park of trees (verse 9), and "el jardín del Edén" is how Spanish speakers name it today. This holds through chapter 3.

source.text: וַיַּצְמַ֞ח יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ מִן־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה כָּל־עֵ֛ץ נֶחְמָ֥ד לְמַרְאֶ֖ה וְט֣וֹב לְמַאֲכָ֑ל וְעֵ֤ץ הַֽחַיִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַגָּ֔ן וְעֵ֕ץ הַדַּ֖עַת ט֥וֹב וָרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And made sprout YHWH God from the ground every tree desirable to sight and good for food, and [the] tree of the life in [the] middle of the garden, and [the] tree of the knowledge [of] good and evil.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made to sprout from the ground every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food, and the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
en.B: Out of the ground {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made every tree grow that is pleasing to look at and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God made all kinds of trees grow out of the ground. They were beautiful to look at, and their fruit was good to eat. In the middle of the garden was the tree that gives life. There was also the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil.

es.L: E hizo brotar {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios del suelo todo árbol agradable a la vista y bueno para comer, y el árbol de la vida en medio del jardín, y el árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal.
es.B: Del suelo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo crecer toda clase de árboles agradables a la vista y buenos para comer. En medio del jardín estaban el árbol de la vida y el árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo crecer del suelo toda clase de árboles. Eran hermosos, y su fruta era buena para comer. En medio del jardín estaba el árbol que da vida. También estaba el árbol que da el conocimiento del bien y del mal.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu fit germer du sol tout arbre désirable à voir et bon pour la nourriture, et l’arbre de la vie au milieu du jardin, et l’arbre de la connaissance du bien et du mal.
fr.B: Du sol, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu fit pousser tous les arbres beaux à regarder et bons à manger. Au milieu du jardin se trouvaient l’arbre de la vie et l’arbre de la connaissance du bien et du mal.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a fait pousser du sol toutes sortes d’arbres. Ils étaient beaux à voir, et leurs fruits étaient bons à manger. Au milieu du jardin, il y avait l’arbre qui donne la vie. Il y avait aussi l’arbre qui fait connaître le bien et le mal.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaotesha kutoka ardhini kila mti wenye kutamanika kwa kuonekana na mwema kwa chakula, na mti wa uzima katikati ya bustani, na mti wa kujua mema na mabaya.
sw.B: Kutoka ardhini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaotesha kila aina ya mti unaopendeza kuutazama na wenye matunda mazuri ya kula. Katikati ya bustani kulikuwa na mti wa uzima, na mti wa kujua mema na mabaya.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaotesha ardhini aina zote za miti. Ilikuwa mizuri kuitazama, na matunda yake yalikuwa mazuri kula. Katikati ya bustani kulikuwa na mti unaotoa uzima. Pia kulikuwa na mti unaomfanya mtu ajue mema na mabaya.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm mọc lên từ đất mọi cây đẹp mắt và tốt để làm thức ăn, và cây của sự sống ở giữa vườn, và cây biết điều thiện và điều ác.
vi.B: Từ đất, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm mọc lên mọi thứ cây đẹp mắt và có trái ăn ngon. Ở giữa vườn có cây của sự sống và cây biết điều thiện và điều ác.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm cho mọi loại cây mọc lên từ đất. Những cây ấy trông rất đẹp, và trái của chúng ăn rất ngon. Ở giữa vườn có cây ban sự sống. Cũng có cây cho biết điều thiện và điều ác.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에서 보기에 탐스럽고 먹기에 좋은 온갖 나무를 돋아나게 하시고, 동산 한가운데에 생명의 나무와 선과 악을 알게 하는 나무를 [돋아나게 하셨다].
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 보기에 아름답고 먹기에 좋은 온갖 나무를 땅에서 자라게 하셨다. 동산 한가운데에는 생명의 나무와 선과 악을 알게 하는 나무가 있었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에서 온갖 나무가 자라나게 하셨다. 그 나무들은 보기에 아름다웠고, 그 열매는 먹기에 좋았다. 동산 한가운데에는 생명을 주는 나무가 있었다. 또 선과 악을 알게 하는 나무도 있었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez brotar do solo toda árvore desejável aos olhos e boa para comer, e a árvore da vida no meio do jardim, e a árvore do conhecimento do bem e do mal.
pt.B: Do solo {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez crescer toda árvore que é bonita de ver e boa para comer. No meio do jardim estavam a árvore da vida e a árvore do conhecimento do bem e do mal.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez crescer do chão todo tipo de árvore. Elas eram bonitas de ver, e as suas frutas eram boas para comer. No meio do jardim estava a árvore que dá vida. Havia também a árvore que dá o conhecimento do bem e do mal.

decisions.choice: the tree of life: a tree whose fruit gives life
decisions.reason: In 3:22 eating from it would let a person live for ever. Proverbs uses the picture for wisdom (Proverbs 3:18), and Revelation 22:2 shows the tree again in the new creation.

decisions.choice: the knowledge of good and evil: deciding for oneself what is good and what is bad
decisions.reason: The phrase can name the ability to judge between good and bad, as a king must (1 Kings 3:9), or that a grown person has and a small child does not (Deuteronomy 1:39). Pairs of opposites can also mean "everything". The story does not define it, but 3:5 and 3:22 show it as something that belongs to God, which human beings take for themselves.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the garden: said of the tree of life, and perhaps of both trees
alternatives: only the tree of life was in the middle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew places the tree of life in the middle of the garden and then adds the tree of knowledge, so it is not clear whether both stood there. In 3:3 the woman speaks of "the tree in the middle of the garden" and means the tree of knowledge, so both may have been there.

decisions.choice: the tree that gives life; the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil
alternatives: the tree of life; the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
decisions.reason: Readable says what each tree does (m1, m2), since "tree of life" alone can sound like a name with no meaning.

decisions.choice: mti wa uzima; mti wa kujua mema na mabaya
alternatives: mti wa ujuzi wa mema na mabaya
decisions.reason: "Uzima" is life itself, the word for eternal life (style guide), where "maisha" is a lifetime; the tree gives life that does not end (3:22, m1). "Kujua" (knowing) keeps the knowledge as something done, deciding for oneself what is good and bad (m2), and is plainer than "ujuzi" (skill, learning).

decisions.choice: "cây biết điều thiện và điều ác"
alternatives: "cây tri thức về thiện và ác"
decisions.reason: The name the Genesis terms note settles for the whole book; Readable says "cây cho biết" (the tree that gives knowledge), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "선과 악을 알게 하는 나무" at every level
decisions.reason: The terms note settles this name for the tree, the same at every level, so that 2:17 and 3:5, 3:22 are heard as the same tree. It says what the tree does, as the English Readable does, and keeps "선과 악" as two words (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: a árvore da vida; a árvore do conhecimento do bem e do mal
alternatives: a árvore da ciência do bem e do mal
decisions.reason: For chapters 2 and 3: the two names are kept as Portuguese readers know them; "conhecimento" is the plain word, where "ciência" in older Bibles now means science. Readable says what each tree does, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְנָהָרּ֙יֹצֵ֣א מֵעֵ֔דֶן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת אֶת־הַגָּ֑ן וּמִשָּׁם֙ יִפָּרֵ֔ד וְהָיָ֖ה לְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה רָאשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And a river [was] going out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.

en.L: And a river was going out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.
en.B: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it split into four branches.
en.R: A river flowed out of Eden and watered the garden. After that it split into four rivers.

es.L: Y un río salía de Edén para regar el jardín, y desde allí se dividía y se convertía en cuatro cabezas.
es.B: De Edén salía un río que regaba el jardín, y desde allí se dividía en cuatro brazos.
es.R: Un río salía de Edén y regaba el jardín. Después se dividía en cuatro ríos.

fr.L: Et un fleuve sortait d’Éden pour arroser le jardin, et de là il se divisait et devenait quatre têtes.
fr.B: D’Éden sortait un fleuve qui arrosait le jardin ; de là, il se partageait en quatre bras.
fr.R: Un fleuve sortait d’Éden et arrosait le jardin. Ensuite, il se divisait en quatre fleuves.

sw.L: Na mto ulikuwa ukitoka Edeni ili kuinywesha bustani, na kutoka huko uligawanyika ukawa vichwa vinne.
sw.B: Mto ulitiririka kutoka Edeni kuinywesha bustani, na kutoka huko ukagawanyika kuwa matawi manne.
sw.R: Mto ulitoka Edeni na kuinywesha bustani. Baadaye ukagawanyika kuwa mito minne.

vi.L: Và một con sông chảy ra từ Ê-đen để tưới vườn, và từ đó nó chia ra và trở thành bốn nhánh.
vi.B: Một con sông chảy ra từ Ê-đen để tưới khu vườn, và từ đó chia thành bốn nhánh.
vi.R: Một con sông chảy ra từ Ê-đen và tưới khu vườn. Sau đó, sông chia ra thành bốn con sông.

ko.L: 그리고 강 하나가 에덴에서 흘러나와 동산을 적셨고, 거기서 갈라져 네 갈래의 머리가 되었다.
ko.B: 강 하나가 에덴에서 흘러나와 동산을 적셨고, 거기서 네 갈래로 갈라졌다.
ko.R: 강 하나가 에덴에서 흘러나와 동산을 적셨다. 그 강은 거기서 네 개의 강으로 갈라졌다.

pt.L: E um rio estava saindo do Éden para regar o jardim, e dali se dividia e se tornava quatro cabeças.
pt.B: Um rio saía do Éden para regar o jardim, e dali se dividia em quatro braços.
pt.R: Um rio saía do Éden e regava o jardim. Depois ele se dividia em quatro rios.

decisions.choice: heads: branches
decisions.reason: The word means "heads". A river's heads can be its sources or the points where it divides. Flowing out from the garden, this river divides into four branches that run out into the known world (verses 11-14).

decisions.choice: a river flowing out to give water: a picture taken up by later scripture
decisions.reason: Later scripture speaks of a river that flows out from where God is and gives life: Psalm 46:5, Ezekiel 47:1-12 and Revelation 22:1-2.

decisions.choice: quatro braços
decisions.reason: "Braço" is the Portuguese word for a branch of a river (m1); Literal keeps "cabeças", the word itself.

source.text: שֵׁ֥ם הָֽאֶחָ֖ד פִּישׁ֑וֹן ה֣וּא הַסֹּבֵ֗ב אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחֲוִילָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] name of the one [is] Pishon; it [is] the [one] going around all [the] land of the Havilah, where there [is] the gold.

en.L: The name of the first [is] Pishon; it [is] the one that goes around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
en.B: The first is named Pishon. It winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
en.R: The first river is called the Pishon. It flows around the whole land of Havilah, where gold is found.

es.L: El nombre del primero [es] Pisón; este [es] el que rodea toda la tierra de Havila, donde hay oro.
es.B: El primero se llama Pisón. Recorre toda la tierra de Havila, donde hay oro.
es.R: El primer río se llama Pisón. Rodea toda la tierra de Havila, donde se encuentra oro.

fr.L: Le nom du premier [est] Pishôn ; c’est lui qui entoure tout le pays de Havila, où il y a de l’or.
fr.B: Le premier s’appelle Pishôn. Il serpente à travers tout le pays de Havila, où l’on trouve de l’or.
fr.R: Le premier fleuve s’appelle le Pishôn. Il fait le tour de tout le pays de Havila, où l’on trouve de l’or.

sw.L: Jina la wa kwanza [ni] Pishoni; ndio unaozunguka nchi yote ya Havila, ambako kuna dhahabu.
sw.B: Wa kwanza unaitwa Pishoni. Unapita katika nchi yote ya Havila, ambako kuna dhahabu.
sw.R: Mto wa kwanza unaitwa Pishoni. Unazunguka nchi yote ya Havila, mahali dhahabu inapopatikana.

vi.L: Tên của [sông] thứ nhất [là] Pi-sôn; nó [là sông] chảy quanh khắp xứ Ha-vi-la, nơi có vàng.
vi.B: Sông thứ nhất tên là Pi-sôn. Sông này chảy quanh khắp xứ Ha-vi-la, là nơi có vàng.
vi.R: Con sông thứ nhất gọi là sông Pi-sôn. Sông ấy chảy quanh khắp xứ Ha-vi-la, là nơi người ta tìm thấy vàng.

ko.L: 첫째의 이름은 비손이니, 그것은 금이 있는 하윌라 온 땅을 돌아 흐르는 것이다.
ko.B: 첫째 강의 이름은 비손이다. 그 강은 금이 나는 하윌라 온 땅을 굽이굽이 흐른다.
ko.R: 첫째 강은 비손이라고 한다. 그 강은 하윌라 온 땅을 돌아 흐르는데, 그곳에서는 금이 난다.

pt.L: O nome do primeiro [é] Pisom; ele [é] o que rodeia toda a terra de Havilá, onde há ouro.
pt.B: O primeiro se chama Pisom. Ele percorre toda a terra de Havilá, onde existe ouro.
pt.R: O primeiro rio se chama Pisom. Ele corre em volta de toda a terra de Havilá, onde se encontra ouro.

decisions.choice: Pishon and Havilah: a river and a land not known today
decisions.reason: The Pishon is not named anywhere else, and where it ran is unknown. Havilah appears among the peoples of Arabia (10:29; 25:18), so the river may have been thought of as lying to the south or east. The writer describes it for readers who knew it, by the gold that made the land famous.

decisions.choice: the first
decisions.reason: Hebrew counts with "one" where English says "first" (as in 1:5).

decisions.choice: Pishôn, Havila; Guihôn, Koush (verse 13); le Tigre, l'Euphrate, l'Assyrie (verse 14)
decisions.reason: The names of the four rivers and their lands take a French transcription of the Hebrew, with the established French names for the Tigris, the Euphrates and Assyria. These forms are used throughout the book.

decisions.choice: Pishoni, Havila; Gihoni, Kushi (verse 13); Tigri, Frati, Ashuru (verse 14)
decisions.reason: The names take their usual Swahili form, ending in a vowel. The third river is called "Tigri", the name Swahili uses for the river today, rather than a transcription of its Hebrew name, as the English says "Tigris" (verse 14, m1). These forms are used throughout the book.

decisions.choice: Pisom, Havilá; Giom, Cuxe, Tigre, Eufrates, Assíria (verses 13-14)
decisions.reason: The names take their usual Brazilian form, which Portuguese readers find in other Bibles and atlases; "Tigre" is the Portuguese name of the river the Hebrew calls Hiddeqel (m1 of verse 14), as the English says "Tigris".

source.text: וּֽזֲהַ֛ב הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִ֖וא ט֑וֹב שָׁ֥ם הַבְּדֹ֖לַח וְאֶ֥בֶן הַשֹּֽׁהַם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] gold of the land the that [is] good; there [is] the bdellium and the stone of the onyx.

en.L: And the gold of that land [is] good; bdellium [is] there, and the onyx stone.
en.B: The gold of that land is good, and aromatic resin and onyx stone are found there as well.
en.R: The gold of that land is of fine quality. Sweet-smelling resin and precious onyx stones are also found there.

es.L: Y el oro de aquella tierra [es] bueno; allí [hay] bedelio y la piedra de ónice.
es.B: El oro de esa tierra es bueno, y allí se encuentran también resina aromática y piedra de ónice.
es.R: El oro de esa tierra es de muy buena calidad. Allí también hay una resina que huele muy bien y piedras preciosas de ónice.

fr.L: Et l’or de ce pays-là [est] bon ; là [se trouvent] le bdellium et la pierre d’onyx.
fr.B: L’or de ce pays est bon, et l’on y trouve aussi de la résine aromatique et de la pierre d’onyx.
fr.R: L’or de ce pays est de très bonne qualité. On y trouve aussi une résine qui sent bon et des pierres précieuses d’onyx.

sw.L: Na dhahabu ya nchi ile [ni] nzuri; pale [kuna] bedola na jiwe la shohamu.
sw.B: Dhahabu ya nchi hiyo ni nzuri, na huko pia kunapatikana utomvu wenye harufu nzuri na jiwe la shohamu.
sw.R: Dhahabu ya nchi hiyo ni safi sana. Huko pia kuna utomvu unaonukia vizuri na vito vya thamani vya shohamu.

vi.L: Và vàng của xứ ấy [thì] tốt; ở đó [có] nhựa thơm và đá hồng mã não.
vi.B: Vàng của xứ ấy rất tốt, và ở đó cũng có nhựa thơm và đá hồng mã não.
vi.R: Vàng ở xứ ấy rất quý. Ở đó người ta cũng tìm thấy nhựa thơm và đá hồng mã não quý giá.

ko.L: 그리고 그 땅의 금은 좋으며, 거기에는 베델리엄과 마노 보석이 [있다].
ko.B: 그 땅의 금은 질이 좋고, 거기에서는 향기로운 나뭇진과 마노 보석도 난다.
ko.R: 그 땅의 금은 아주 좋다. 거기에서는 향기가 좋은 나뭇진과 값진 마노 보석도 난다.

pt.L: E o ouro daquela terra [é] bom; ali [há] o bdélio e a pedra de ônix.
pt.B: O ouro dessa terra é bom, e ali também se encontram resina aromática e pedra de ônix.
pt.R: O ouro dessa terra é de ótima qualidade. Ali também se encontram resina perfumada e pedras preciosas de ônix.

decisions.choice: bdellium: a fragrant resin, or perhaps a pearl
decisions.reason: The word appears again only in Numbers 11:7, where manna looks like it. It is usually taken to be a sweet-smelling gum from a tree, valued in the ancient world; some have taken it to be a pearl.

decisions.choice: onyx: a precious stone, not certainly identified
decisions.reason: Onyx stones were set on the high priest's garments (Exodus 28:9-12, 20). The exact stone is not known. Gold and precious stones later adorn the tabernacle, one of several links between the garden and the place where God lives among his people.

decisions.choice: aromatic resin (B); sweet-smelling resin (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bdellium", the traditional word; Balanced and Readable say what it most likely was (m1).

decisions.choice: bedola (L); utomvu wenye harufu nzuri (B, R); shohamu
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional transcription "bedola", as the English keeps "bdellium"; Balanced and Readable say what it most likely was, a sweet-smelling tree resin (m1). The stone is not certainly identified (m2), so its Hebrew name "shohamu" is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: "nhựa thơm" for bdellium at every level
decisions.reason: Bdellium is most likely a sweet-smelling gum resin (m1); "nhũ hương" means frankincense, a different resin, so every level says "nhựa thơm", as Numbers 11:7 does.

source.text: וְשֵֽׁם־הַנָּהָ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י גִּיח֑וֹן ה֣וּא הַסּוֹבֵ֔ב אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ כּֽוּשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of the river the second [is] Gihon; it [is] the [one] going around all [the] land of Cush.

en.L: And the name of the second river [is] Gihon; it [is] the one that goes around the whole land of Cush.
en.B: The second river is named Gihon. It winds through the whole land of Cush.
en.R: The second river is called the Gihon. It flows around the whole land of Cush.

es.L: Y el nombre del segundo río [es] Gihón; este [es] el que rodea toda la tierra de Cus.
es.B: El segundo río se llama Gihón. Recorre toda la tierra de Cus.
es.R: El segundo río se llama Gihón. Rodea toda la tierra de Cus.

fr.L: Et le nom du second fleuve [est] Guihôn ; c’est lui qui entoure tout le pays de Koush.
fr.B: Le deuxième fleuve s’appelle Guihôn. Il serpente à travers tout le pays de Koush.
fr.R: Le deuxième fleuve s’appelle le Guihôn. Il fait le tour de tout le pays de Koush.

sw.L: Na jina la mto wa pili [ni] Gihoni; ndio unaozunguka nchi yote ya Kushi.
sw.B: Mto wa pili unaitwa Gihoni. Unapita katika nchi yote ya Kushi.
sw.R: Mto wa pili unaitwa Gihoni. Unazunguka nchi yote ya Kushi.

vi.L: Và tên của sông thứ hai [là] Ghi-hôn; nó [là sông] chảy quanh khắp xứ Cút.
vi.B: Sông thứ hai tên là Ghi-hôn. Sông này chảy quanh khắp xứ Cút.
vi.R: Con sông thứ hai gọi là sông Ghi-hôn. Sông ấy chảy quanh khắp xứ Cút.

ko.L: 그리고 둘째 강의 이름은 기혼이니, 그것은 구스 온 땅을 돌아 흐르는 것이다.
ko.B: 둘째 강의 이름은 기혼이다. 그 강은 구스 온 땅을 굽이굽이 흐른다.
ko.R: 둘째 강은 기혼이라고 한다. 그 강은 구스 온 땅을 돌아 흐른다.

pt.L: E o nome do segundo rio [é] Giom; ele [é] o que rodeia toda a terra de Cuxe.
pt.B: O segundo rio se chama Giom. Ele percorre toda a terra de Cuxe.
pt.R: O segundo rio se chama Giom. Ele corre em volta de toda a terra de Cuxe.

decisions.choice: Gihon and Cush: probably a land to the east here, though Cush usually means the land south of Egypt
alternatives: Cush as Ethiopia, with the Gihon as the Nile
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Cush usually names the land south of Egypt, roughly today's Sudan (Isaiah 18:1). But 10:8 links Cush with Nimrod, whose kingdom was in Mesopotamia, and the name here may point east, near the Tigris and Euphrates. Gihon is also the name of the spring of Jerusalem (1 Kings 1:33).

source.text: וְשֵׁ֨ם הַנָּהָ֤ר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ חִדֶּ֔קֶל ה֥וּא הַֽהֹלֵ֖ךְ קִדְמַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר וְהַנָּהָ֥ר הָֽרְבִיעִ֖י ה֥וּא פְרָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of the river the third [is] Tigris; it [is] the [one] going east of Assyria. And the river the fourth, it [is] Euphrates.

en.L: And the name of the third river [is] Tigris; it [is] the one that goes east of Assyria. And the fourth river, it [is the] Euphrates.
en.B: The third river is named Tigris. It runs east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
en.R: The third river is called the Tigris. It flows along the east side of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.

es.L: Y el nombre del tercer río [es] Tigris; este [es] el que va al oriente de Asiria. Y el cuarto río, ese [es el] Éufrates.
es.B: El tercer río se llama Tigris. Corre al este de Asiria. Y el cuarto río es el Éufrates.
es.R: El tercer río se llama Tigris. Pasa por el lado este de Asiria. El cuarto río es el Éufrates.

fr.L: Et le nom du troisième fleuve [est le] Tigre ; c’est lui qui va à l’est de l’Assyrie. Et le quatrième fleuve, c’est l’Euphrate.
fr.B: Le troisième fleuve s’appelle le Tigre. Il coule à l’est de l’Assyrie. Et le quatrième fleuve est l’Euphrate.
fr.R: Le troisième fleuve s’appelle le Tigre. Il passe du côté est de l’Assyrie. Le quatrième fleuve est l’Euphrate.

sw.L: Na jina la mto wa tatu [ni] Tigri; ndio unaokwenda upande wa mashariki wa Ashuru. Na mto wa nne, huo [ni] Frati.
sw.B: Mto wa tatu unaitwa Tigri. Unatiririka upande wa mashariki wa Ashuru. Na mto wa nne ni Frati.
sw.R: Mto wa tatu unaitwa Tigri. Unapita upande wa mashariki wa Ashuru. Mto wa nne ni Frati.

vi.L: Và tên của sông thứ ba [là] Ti-gơ-rơ; nó [là sông] chảy về phía đông A-si-ri. Và sông thứ tư, nó [là sông] Ơ-phơ-rát.
vi.B: Sông thứ ba tên là Ti-gơ-rơ. Sông này chảy về phía đông A-si-ri. Và sông thứ tư là sông Ơ-phơ-rát.
vi.R: Con sông thứ ba gọi là sông Ti-gơ-rơ. Sông ấy chảy dọc theo phía đông xứ A-si-ri. Con sông thứ tư là sông Ơ-phơ-rát.

ko.L: 그리고 셋째 강의 이름은 티그리스이니, 그것은 앗시리아 동쪽으로 흐르는 것이다. 그리고 넷째 강, 그것은 유프라테스이다.
ko.B: 셋째 강의 이름은 티그리스이다. 그 강은 앗시리아 동쪽으로 흐른다. 그리고 넷째 강은 유프라테스이다.
ko.R: 셋째 강은 티그리스라고 한다. 그 강은 앗시리아의 동쪽을 따라 흐른다. 넷째 강은 유프라테스이다.

pt.L: E o nome do terceiro rio [é] Tigre; ele [é] o que vai a leste da Assíria. E o quarto rio, ele [é o] Eufrates.
pt.B: O terceiro rio se chama Tigre. Ele corre a leste da Assíria. E o quarto rio é o Eufrates.
pt.R: O terceiro rio se chama Tigre. Ele passa pelo lado leste da Assíria. O quarto rio é o Eufrates.

decisions.choice: Tigris and Euphrates: the two great rivers of Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name of the third river, Hiddeqel, is the Tigris (Daniel 10:4). With the Euphrates, which needs no description, it places the garden in or near Mesopotamia, the land between these two rivers. The four rivers together reach to the edges of the world the first readers knew.

decisions.choice: east of Assyria
decisions.reason: The word can mean "east of" or "in front of". The Tigris runs through the heart of Assyria, and the phrase may describe it as seen from the writer's own land.

decisions.choice: "티그리스", "앗시리아", "유프라테스"
decisions.reason: The modern names, as the Korean Psalms (Psalm 83) and Revelation (9:14) already write Assyria and the Euphrates; the forms of older Bibles are not used.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֛ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֑ם וַיַּנִּחֵ֣הוּ בְגַן־עֵ֔דֶן לְעָבְדָ֖הּ וּלְשָׁמְרָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And took YHWH God the man and put him in [the] garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God took the man and placed him in the garden of Eden to work it and to keep it.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

decisions.choice: placed: settled, gave a place of rest
decisions.reason: The verb is not the one used for "put" in verse 8. It comes from the word for rest, and is used for God giving his people rest in their land (Deuteronomy 3:20) and for setting something before the LORD (Exodus 16:33-34).

decisions.choice: to work it and keep it: to tend the garden and to guard it
alternatives: to farm it and protect it, with no wider sense
decisions.reason: The first verb means to work or to serve; the second means to keep, watch over or guard. The same two verbs describe the work of the Levites at the tabernacle (Numbers 3:7-8), so the garden is pictured as a holy place and the man as its keeper. Work belongs to the good world from the start; it is not a result of the curse in 3:17-19. The word "it" is feminine in Hebrew, though "garden" is masculine, and may point back to "the ground" (verse 5).

decisions.choice: settled him

Balanced and Readable say "cultivar" and "cuidar", the everyday words for tending a garden.

decisions.choice: pour le travailler et pour le garder

decisions.choice: you shall not eat: a lasting prohibition

decisions.choice: on the day you eat from it you will surely die: from that day death is certain
alternatives: you will die before that day ends
you will die inwardly that day
decisions.reason: "In the day" often means simply "when" (2:4). The doubled verb, "dying you will die", is the form of a death sentence (1 Kings 2:37, 42; Ezekiel 3:18). Some readers also see a death on that day in their broken relationship with God.

decisions.choice: not good: the first thing in creation called not good
decisions.reason: Throughout chapter 1 God saw that what he made was good. Here, for the first time, something is not good: the man alone. Human beings are made for companionship.

decisions.choice: helper: one who gives help the other needs, not a lesser assistant
decisions.reason: The word does not suggest a lower rank: it is most often used of God himself as the helper of his people (Exodus 18:4; Psalm 33:20; 121:1-2). It names someone who gives help that is needed.

decisions.choice: corresponding to him: like him and facing him, his counterpart
decisions.reason: The phrase joins "like" and "in front of, opposite". The helper will be his equal and his match, someone who stands face to face with him, as no animal can (verse 20).

decisions.choice: partner
decisions.reason: In plain English "helper" can suggest a lesser assistant, which the Hebrew does not mean (m2), so Readable says "partner".

decisions.choice: who matches him
decisions.reason: Balanced says "matches" to keep both sides of the phrase, likeness and facing (m3).

decisions.choice: una ayuda (L, B); alguien que lo ayude y lo acompañe (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "ayudante" names an assistant under someone's direction, which the Hebrew does not mean (m2). The noun "ayuda" carries no rank and is the word Spanish uses for God's help ("mi ayuda viene del SEÑOR", Psalm 121:2), as the Hebrew word is. Where English Readable says "partner", Spanish Readable can keep the idea of help, since the verb "ayudar" does not suggest a lesser helper; it avoids "compañera", which would name the woman before she is made (verse 22).

decisions.choice: que le corresponda (L); a su medida (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Idónea", the traditional Spanish word here, now means suitable or qualified, and says nothing of likeness or facing. "A su medida" (made to his measure) says that the helper matches him, his equal and counterpart (m3). Literal says "que le corresponda", close to the English Literal. The same wording returns in verse 20.

decisions.choice: une aide qui lui corresponde (L); une aide qui soit à sa mesure (B); quelqu'un qui l'accompagne et qui soit vraiment fait pour lui (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase says both likeness and facing (m3). Balanced says "à sa mesure", made to match him; Readable avoids "aide", which can sound like an assistant (m2), as the English Readable says "partner".

decisions.choice: msaidizi (L, B); mwenzi (R)
decisions.reason: "Msaidizi" is one who helps, the plain sense of the word, which elsewhere names God as the helper of his people (m2). Readable says "mwenzi", a partner or companion, as the English Readable says "partner", so that the word is not heard as a lesser assistant.

decisions.choice: "người giúp đỡ tương xứng" (L), "người giúp đỡ xứng hợp" (B), "người bạn đời thật hợp" (R)
decisions.reason: The helper gives the help the other needs and is not a lesser assistant (m2), so "phụ" (assistant) is avoided. Readable says "bạn đời" (life partner), as the English Readable says "partner"; like the English choice it says more than the word, so it is marked uncertain.

decisions.choice: "그와 마주 서는 돕는 이" (L); "꼭 맞는 돕는 짝" (B); "꼭 맞는 짝" (R)
decisions.reason: The helper is one who gives help the other cannot do without, not a lesser assistant, and is "like him, facing him" (meaning decisions m2, m3). "조력자" would sound like an assistant; "돕는 배필" is the wording of older Bibles. Literal keeps the picture of facing; Balanced and Readable say "짝", one who matches him, as the English says "partner" at Readable.

decisions.choice: uma ajuda que lhe corresponda (L); alguém que o ajude e que lhe corresponda (B); alguém que seja o par certo para ele (R)
alternatives: uma auxiliadora que lhe seja idônea
decisions.reason: The feminine nouns "auxiliadora" and "ajudadora" sound like a subordinate assistant, which the word does not mean: it is used most often of God as his people's helper (m2). "Uma ajuda" and "alguém que o ajude" keep the help without the rank; "que lhe corresponda" keeps likeness and facing (m3). Readable says "o par certo", a plain word for a counterpart, as the English Readable says "partner". The same words return in verse 20.

source.text: וַיִּצֶר֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים מִן־הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה כָּל־חַיַּ֤ת הַשָּׂדֶה֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיָּבֵא֙ אֶל־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם לִרְא֖וֹת מַה־יִּקְרָא־ל֑וֹ וְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקְרָא־ל֧וֹ הָֽאָדָ֛ם נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה ה֥וּא שְׁמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And formed YHWH God from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and brought [them] to the man to see what he would call it; and all that called it the man, living creature, that [was] its name.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the heavens, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought [them] to the man to see what he would call each one; and whatever the man called each living creature, that [was] its name.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God formed out of the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would name them. Whatever the man called each living creature, that became its name.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} God made all the wild animals and all the birds out of the ground. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them to the man to see what names he would give them. Whatever the man called each living thing, that was its name.

es.L: Y formó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios del suelo todo animal del campo y toda ave de los cielos, y [los] trajo al hombre para ver cómo llamaría a cada uno; y como el hombre llamó a cada criatura viviente, ese [fue] su nombre.
es.B: Así que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios formó del suelo todos los animales salvajes y todas las aves del cielo, y se los llevó al hombre para ver qué nombre les pondría. El nombre que el hombre le dio a cada ser viviente, ese fue su nombre.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo del suelo todos los animales salvajes y todas las aves. Luego se los llevó al hombre para ver qué nombres les pondría. El nombre que el hombre le daba a cada ser vivo, ese era su nombre.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu forma du sol tout animal des champs et tout oiseau des cieux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] amena à l’homme pour voir comment il appellerait chacun ; et quel que soit le nom dont l’homme appela chaque être vivant, ce [fut] son nom.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu façonna donc du sol tous les animaux sauvages et tous les oiseaux du ciel, et les amena à l’homme pour voir quel nom il leur donnerait. Le nom que l’homme donna à chaque être vivant devint son nom.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a fait avec le sol tous les animaux sauvages et tous les oiseaux. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a amenés à l’homme pour voir quels noms il allait leur donner. Le nom que l’homme donnait à chaque être vivant, c’était son nom.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akafinyanga kutoka ardhini kila mnyama wa shambani na kila ndege wa mbinguni, akawaleta kwa mtu ili aone atamwita kila mmoja jina gani; na kila jina ambalo mtu alimwita kila kiumbe hai, hilo [likawa] jina lake.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akafinyanga kutoka ardhini kila mnyama wa porini na kila ndege wa angani, akawaleta kwa mtu ili aone atawapa majina gani. Jina lolote ambalo mtu alimpa kila kiumbe hai, hilo likawa jina lake.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akafanya kutoka ardhini wanyama wote wa porini na ndege wote. Kisha akawaleta kwa mtu ili aone atawapa majina gani. Jina lolote mtu alilompa kila kiumbe hai, ndilo lililokuwa jina lake.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời nắn từ đất mọi thú vật của đồng ruộng và mọi chim trên trời, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đem [chúng] đến với con người để xem người sẽ gọi mỗi con là gì; và hễ con người gọi mỗi sinh vật sống là gì, thì đó [là] tên của nó.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời nắn từ đất mọi thú rừng và mọi chim trên trời, rồi đem chúng đến với con người để xem người sẽ đặt tên cho chúng là gì. Hễ con người gọi mỗi sinh vật sống là gì, thì đó trở thành tên của nó.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời lấy đất làm ra mọi thú rừng và mọi loài chim. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đem chúng đến với người đàn ông để xem người sẽ đặt tên cho chúng là gì. Người gọi mỗi sinh vật là gì, thì đó là tên của nó.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에서 들의 모든 짐승과 하늘의 모든 새를 빚으시고, 그 사람이 그것들을 무엇이라고 부르는지 보시려고 [그것들을] 그 사람에게로 데려오셨다. 그리고 그 사람이 각 살아 있는 생물을 무엇이라고 부르든지, 그것이 그 이름이 되었다.
ko.B: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에서 모든 들짐승과 하늘의 모든 새를 빚으시고, 그 사람이 그것들의 이름을 무엇이라고 짓는지 보시려고 그에게 데려오셨다. 그 사람이 살아 있는 생물 하나하나를 부르는 대로 그것이 그 이름이 되었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 땅에서 모든 들짐승과 모든 새를 만드셨다. 그리고 그 사람이 그것들에게 어떤 이름을 붙이는지 보시려고 그것들을 그에게 데려오셨다. 그 사람이 살아 있는 것 하나하나를 부르는 대로 그것이 그 이름이 되었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus formou do solo todo animal do campo e toda ave dos céus, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} [os] trouxe ao homem para ver como ele chamaria cada um; e como quer que o homem chamasse cada ser vivente, esse [era] o seu nome.
pt.B: Assim {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus formou do solo todos os animais selvagens e todas as aves do céu e os trouxe ao homem para ver que nomes ele lhes daria. O nome que o homem deu a cada ser vivo, esse passou a ser o seu nome.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez do chão todos os animais selvagens e todas as aves. Depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os levou até o homem para ver que nomes o homem daria a eles. O nome que o homem deu a cada ser vivo, esse ficou sendo o seu nome.

decisions.choice: formed: told here in the order of this story, not as a new order of creation
alternatives: had formed (before the man was made)
decisions.reason: The verb form usually tells the next event, which would put the making of the animals after the man, unlike chapter 1. It can also look back ("had formed"). Either way, this account is told around the man and his need: the animals are brought to him as possible companions, and its order is the order of the story.

decisions.choice: to see what he would call them: the man names the animals
decisions.reason: In chapter 1 God names day, night, sky, land and seas (1:5, 8, 10). Here he lets the man name the animals, a sign of the rule given to human beings in 1:26-28, and waits "to see" what he will do.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א הָֽאָדָ֜ם שֵׁמ֗וֹת לְכָל־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּלְע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּלְאָדָ֕ם לֹֽא־מָצָ֥א עֵ֖זֶר כְּנֶגְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And called the man names to all the livestock and to [the] bird[s] of the heavens and to every animal of the field, but for [the] man not he found a helper as opposite him.

en.L: And the man gave names to all the livestock and to the birds of the heavens and to every animal of the field, but for the man he did not find a helper corresponding to him.
en.B: The man gave names to all the livestock, the birds of the sky and every wild animal. But no helper who matched him was found for the man.
en.R: So the man gave names to all the farm animals, the birds and the wild animals. But none of them was the right partner for the man.

es.L: Y puso el hombre nombres a todo el ganado y a las aves de los cielos y a todo animal del campo, pero para el hombre no halló una ayuda que le correspondiera.
es.B: El hombre les puso nombre a todo el ganado, a las aves del cielo y a todos los animales salvajes. Pero para el hombre no se encontró una ayuda a su medida.
es.R: Así que el hombre les puso nombre a todos los animales de la granja, a las aves y a los animales salvajes. Pero ninguno de ellos era alguien a su medida que pudiera acompañarlo.

fr.L: Et l’homme donna des noms à tout le bétail et aux oiseaux des cieux et à tout animal des champs, mais pour l’homme il ne trouva pas d’aide qui lui corresponde.
fr.B: L’homme donna des noms à tout le bétail, aux oiseaux du ciel et à tous les animaux sauvages. Mais pour l’homme, on ne trouva pas d’aide qui soit à sa mesure.
fr.R: Ainsi, l’homme a donné un nom à tous les animaux de la ferme, aux oiseaux et aux animaux sauvages. Mais aucun d’eux n’était vraiment fait pour l’accompagner.

sw.L: Na mtu akawapa majina wanyama wote wa kufugwa, na ndege wa mbinguni, na kila mnyama wa shambani, lakini kwa ajili ya mtu hakupata msaidizi anayemfaa, aliye sawa naye.
sw.B: Mtu akawapa majina wanyama wote wa kufugwa, ndege wa angani na kila mnyama wa porini. Lakini kwa ajili ya mtu hakupatikana msaidizi anayemfaa kikamilifu.
sw.R: Basi mtu akawapa majina wanyama wote wa kufugwa, ndege, na wanyama wa porini. Lakini hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyekuwa mwenzi anayemfaa.

vi.L: Và con người đặt tên cho mọi gia súc, và cho chim trên trời, và cho mọi thú vật của đồng ruộng, nhưng cho con người thì không tìm được một người giúp đỡ tương xứng với người.
vi.B: Con người đặt tên cho mọi gia súc, mọi chim trên trời và mọi thú rừng. Nhưng không tìm được cho con người một người giúp đỡ xứng hợp với người.
vi.R: Vậy người đàn ông đặt tên cho mọi gia súc, mọi loài chim và mọi thú rừng. Nhưng không con nào trong số ấy là người bạn đời hợp với người.

ko.L: 그리고 그 사람이 모든 가축과 하늘의 새와 들의 모든 짐승에게 이름을 지어 주었다. 그러나 사람을 위해서는 그와 마주 서는 돕는 이를 찾지 못하였다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 모든 가축과 하늘의 새와 모든 들짐승에게 이름을 지어 주었다. 그러나 그 사람에게 꼭 맞는 돕는 짝은 찾을 수 없었다.
ko.R: 그래서 그 사람은 모든 집짐승과 새와 들짐승에게 이름을 지어 주었다. 그러나 그것들 가운데 그 사람에게 꼭 맞는 짝은 없었다.

pt.L: E o homem deu nomes a todos os animais domésticos e às aves dos céus e a todo animal do campo, mas para o homem ele não achou uma ajuda que lhe correspondesse.
pt.B: O homem deu nomes a todos os animais domésticos, às aves do céu e a todos os animais selvagens. Mas para o homem não se achou ninguém que o ajudasse e que lhe correspondesse.
pt.R: Assim o homem deu nomes a todos os animais de criação, às aves e aos animais selvagens. Mas nenhum deles era o par certo para o homem.

decisions.choice: for the man: not yet the name Adam
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew vowels give the word without the article, so it can be read as the name Adam, and some translations begin to use the name here. But the story goes on to speak of "the man" in the next verses, and the name is plainly used only from 4:25, so it is taken as "the man".

decisions.choice: he did not find: the one who looks is not named
decisions.reason: The verb is "he found", with no subject named. It may be the man, who finds no partner among the animals, or God.

decisions.choice: was found
decisions.reason: Balanced leaves the finder unnamed, as the Hebrew does (m2), by saying "was found".

source.text: וַיַּפֵּל֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀תַּרְדֵּמָ֛ה עַל־הָאָדָ֖ם וַיִּישָׁ֑ן וַיִּקַּ֗ח אַחַת֙ מִצַּלְעֹתָ֔יו וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר בָּשָׂ֖ר תַּחְתֶּֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And caused to fall YHWH God a deep sleep on the man, and he slept; and he took one from his sides, and closed flesh in its place.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man, and he slept; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took one of his sides and closed up [the] flesh in its place.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the man fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made the man fall into a deep sleep. While he was sleeping, God took out one of his ribs. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} closed up the place with flesh.

es.L: E hizo caer {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios un sueño profundo sobre el hombre, y durmió; y tomó uno de sus costados y cerró [la] carne en su lugar.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo caer al hombre en un sueño profundo, y mientras dormía, le sacó una de las costillas y cerró la carne en su lugar.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios hizo que el hombre se quedara profundamente dormido. Mientras dormía, Dios le sacó una de las costillas. Después cerró con carne el lugar.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu fit tomber un sommeil profond sur l’homme, et il s’endormit ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit l’un de ses côtés et referma [la] chair à sa place.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu plongea l’homme dans un sommeil profond, et pendant qu’il dormait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui prit une côte et referma la chair à cet endroit.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} Dieu a fait tomber l’homme dans un sommeil très profond. Pendant qu’il dormait, Dieu lui a retiré une côte. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a refermé l’endroit avec de la chair.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akaangusha usingizi mzito juu ya mtu, naye akalala; akachukua mojawapo ya mbavu zake, akafunga nyama mahali pake.
sw.B: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamfanya mtu alale usingizi mzito, na alipokuwa amelala, akaondoa mojawapo ya mbavu zake, akaziba mahali pale kwa nyama.
sw.R: Basi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu akamfanya mtu alale usingizi mzito sana. Alipokuwa amelala, Mungu akatoa ubavu wake mmoja. Kisha akaziba mahali pale kwa nyama.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm cho một giấc ngủ say giáng trên con người, và người ngủ; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy một bên sườn của người và khép thịt lại ở chỗ đó.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm cho con người ngủ say, và trong khi người ngủ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy một xương sườn của người rồi khép thịt lại ở chỗ ấy.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời làm cho người đàn ông ngủ say. Trong khi người đang ngủ, Đức Chúa Trời lấy ra một xương sườn của người. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lấy thịt khép chỗ ấy lại.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람 위에 깊은 잠이 내리게 하시니 그가 잠들었다. 그리고 그의 옆구리 가운데 하나를 취하시고, 그 자리를 살로 닫으셨다.
ko.B: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람을 깊이 잠들게 하시고, 그가 잠든 사이에 그의 갈비뼈 하나를 꺼내시고 그 자리를 살로 메우셨다.
ko.R: 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 하나님께서 그 사람을 깊이 잠들게 하셨다. 그가 자고 있는 동안 하나님께서 그의 갈비뼈 하나를 꺼내셨다. 그리고 그 자리를 살로 메우셨다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez cair um sono profundo sobre o homem, e ele dormiu; e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tomou um dos lados dele e fechou [com] carne o lugar dele.
pt.B: Assim {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez o homem cair num sono profundo e, enquanto ele dormia, tirou uma das costelas dele e fechou a carne no lugar dela.
pt.R: Então {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} Deus fez o homem cair num sono profundo. Enquanto o homem dormia, Deus tirou uma das costelas dele. Depois {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fechou o lugar com carne.

decisions.choice: deep sleep: a heavy sleep sent by God
decisions.reason: The word is used of a sleep that God sends, sometimes with a vision (15:12; 1 Samuel 26:12). The man does not see what God does.

decisions.choice: one of his sides: a rib, or one side of him
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the word means the side of something: of the ark of the covenant or of a hill (Exodus 25:12; 2 Samuel 16:13), and the side rooms of the temple (1 Kings 6:5). Here it may be a rib, or a whole side of the man. Either way, the woman is made from the man's own body, "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh" (verse 23).

decisions.choice: sides (L); ribs (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "side", the word's usual sense; Balanced and Readable say "rib", the traditional reading and the likelier one here (m2). The same applies in verse 22.

decisions.choice: mbavu, ubavu
decisions.reason: Swahili "ubavu" (plural "mbavu") means both the side of the body and a rib, as the Hebrew word can (m2), so one word serves at every level and Swahili needs no Literal "side" against a Balanced "rib" (r-en-1). The same holds in verse 22.

decisions.choice: "một bên sườn" (L), "một xương sườn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "side", and here most likely a rib (m2). Literal's "bên sườn" keeps the wider word, as the English Literal says "sides".

decisions.choice: fechou [com] carne o lugar dele
alternatives: fechou a carne no seu lugar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "closed flesh in its place"; Portuguese needs "com" to say that flesh filled the place, so Literal brackets it. Literal says "um dos lados dele" and Balanced and Readable "uma das costelas dele", as the English (m2); "dele" makes plain whose side, where "seus" could be read as God's.

source.text: וַיִּבֶן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀אֶֽת־הַצֵּלָ֛ע אֲשֶׁר־לָקַ֥ח מִן־הָֽאָדָ֖ם לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיְבִאֶ֖הָ אֶל־הָֽאָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And built YHWH God the side which he had taken from the man into a woman, and brought her to the man.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God built the side that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken from the man into a woman, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought her to the man.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God built a woman out of the rib {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken from the man, and brought her to him.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God made a woman from the rib {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had taken out of the man. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought her to the man.

es.L: Y construyó {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios, del costado que había tomado del hombre, una mujer, y la trajo al hombre.
